links.outcome: Output quality of knowledge-graph-grounded RAG versus baseline models on RAGAS and expert evaluation
links.effect: MAGR-TCM significantly outperformed all baseline models on RAGAS automatic evaluation and expert human evaluation; authors state it mitigates generative hallucinations.
links.quote: Experimental results demonstrate that MAGR-TCM significantly outperforms all baseline models on both RAGAS automatic evaluation and expert human evaluation.

links.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity for distinguishing self-treatable conditions from those needing urgent hospital care
links.effect: 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity on the safety test set.
links.quote: The model achieved 100% sensitivity and specificity on the safety test set, further validating its practical utility in home health settings and its ability to distinguish self-treatable conditions from those requiring urgent hospital care.

unlisted_practices: Constructing an expert-supervised domain knowledge graph to support multi-agent retrieval-augmented generation

screen.reason: The paper introduces and benchmarks a novel multi-agent RAG system (MAGR-TCM) for TCM gynecology consultation and triage. While it tests safety/hallucination mitigation, it is presenting and evaluating a new model/architecture rather than evaluating an organizational deployment practice or guardrail added to an existing tool.
